content: Hello, I'm curious about the status of the TODO in Mathlib.Algebra.CharZero.Defs (it's about unifying CharZero with CharP). Is there anyone working on it?
(docs#CharZero, docs#CharP)
These to me seem like different things with an unfortunate name clash. I don't think unifying them would be desirable.

Well I mean, these definitions have been extended beyond where they are commonly used in maths, and you can ask how valid they are for non-rings!

NB I have no idea if experts already thought about these definitions, or if they were generalised naively.
My own mental model of these typeclasses is that you use CharP when you're talking about rings, and you use CharZero for the boilerplate lemmas on Nat.cast that gives you.

Violeta Hernández said:

These to me seem like different things with an unfortunate name clash. I don't think unifying them would be desirable.

i think they actually are not as clashing as they seem:
for non-zero p, with CharP R p, Nat.cast will be injective on Set.Iio p : Set Nat, and therefore Nat.cast will lift to a ringhom embedding of ZMod p into R.
see CharP.cast_eq_iff_mod_eq for a proof which assumes IsLeftCancelAdd R instead of 0 < p, or the following (not in mathlib) proof:

code

import Mathlib

variable {R : Type*} [AddMonoidWithOne R] (p : ℕ) [CharP R p] (hp : 0 < p)


lemma CharP.cast_eq_iff_mod_eq (n m : ℕ) (heq : (n : R) = (m : R)) : n % p = m % p := by
  wlog! h : n % p ≤ m % p generalizing n m
  · exact (this m n heq.symm h.le).symm
  have : (n : R) + (p - n % p : R) = 0 := by
    rw [← Nat.cast_add, CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff, ← Nat.add_sub_assoc (Nat.mod_lt _ hp).le, add_comm, Nat.add_sub_assoc (Nat.mod_le _ _), Nat.dvd_add_self_left]
    exact Nat.dvd_sub_mod _
  rw [heq, ← Nat.cast_add, CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff, ← Nat.add_sub_assoc (Nat.mod_lt _ hp).le, add_comm, Nat.add_sub_assoc, Nat.dvd_add_self_left] at this
  rw [Nat.dvd_iff_mod_eq_zero, ← Nat.div_add_mod m p,
    Nat.add_sub_assoc h, Nat.mul_add_mod_self_left] at this
  rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt, Nat.sub_eq_zero_iff_le] at this
  exact le_antisymm h this
  apply lt_of_le_of_lt _ (Nat.mod_lt m hp)
  exact Nat.sub_le (m % p) (n % p)
  exact le_trans h (Nat.mod_le _ _)
it's actually sensible to unify these.
We already have https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Counterexamples/CharPZeroNeCharZero.lean by @Damiano Testa
I mean, if you are interested in weird stuff about these notions

indeed, they aren't the same, but arguably we do want CharP R 0 to be equivalent to the current CharZero R

for non-zero p, with CharP R p, Nat.cast will be injective on Set.Iio p : Set Nat, and therefore Nat.cast will lift to a ringhom embedding of ZMod p into R.

I'm surprised this works with the bare assumption of AddMonoidWithOne. So, the idea would be to make CharP R p mean that Nat.cast is injective on Iio p for p ≠ 0, and on ℕ otherwise?
up to logical equivalence, yes. Ideally there's a different, more homogenous phrasing
Nat.cast a = Nat.cast b iff p ∣ a - b?

Violeta Hernández said:

Nat.cast a = Nat.cast b implies p ∣ a - b?

Or a % p = b % p due to how subtraction in Nat works. But then it's docs#CharP.cast_eq_iff_mod_eq.
we could also consider using (Nat.cast a : ZMod p) = Nat.cast b
It feels somehow weird, as we are also proving a CharP instances on ZMod p later on; but this is personal as I don't think it causes any real issue.

In the end, this is probably the way to make the refactor simplest? And all the other ones are logically equivalent anyway.
Actually I take that back, it's wrong when a <= b! We need the % version
Yeah, I meant a - b in the sense of integer subtraction. Wasn't sure how to write a = b (mod p) in Lean.
There is fancy notation for exactly this in Mathlib, which we could consider

Gian Cordana Sanjaya ha dicho:

Violeta Hernández said:

Nat.cast a = Nat.cast b implies p ∣ a - b?

Or a % p = b % p due to how subtraction in Nat works. But then it's docs#CharP.cast_eq_iff_mod_eq.

We can actually use this theorem to prove CharZero R ↔ CharP R 0 under the assumption of AddMonoidWithOne + IsLeftCancelAdd rather than the stronger AddGroupWithOne. #38289
So they're not really all that different after all.

Violeta Hernández said:

Yeah, I meant a - b in the sense of integer subtraction. Wasn't sure how to write a = b (mod p) in Lean.

Use docs#Nat.ModEq: a ≡ b [MOD p].
I can't forsee any qualms with this unification. Surely there's no one who cares about the characteristic of a monoid where addition isn't even cancellative?
...I guess there's ordinals and cardinals, but both of those are the stronger (and arguably correct) CharZero, so it should be fine.
Yeah, I think at least one of these definitions should be changed. Using the stronger notion makes sense to me. The weaker notion can be a theorem.
I'll try making the PR in the next few days (unless someone else wants to?)
i was thinking Gian Cordana Sanjaya asked if someone was working on it with the intention to do it if not?
I was thinking of that, but I can pass it up to anyone since doing this will break some parts of mathlib for a while, I'm just not very confident on this. Or should I just try?

Nope, after trying for a while, I'll pass it to someone else :smiling_face_with_tear:

Note: doing this change means ringChar would require IsLeftCancelAdd, which shouldn't be surprising.
I feel like it should be defined to equal the exponent of the underlying additive group, docs#Addmonoid.exponent.

That wouldn't necessarily work in an AddMonoidWithOne although it works with Ring (and I believe it works even with NonAssocSemiring). For example consider Fin 2 × ℤ but with the one element being (1, 0) rather than (1, 1).
If 1 is an AddUnit then the characteristic can be the order of 1
but 1 is not always an AddUnit
